what_this_is: The record of provisioning Daniel's REAL vault skills into his REAL harness skill directories (~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills) and proving discovery with a fresh process of each installed CLI. scripts/emit-evidence.sh cannot run this: it mutates the operator's own harness directories, so it is recorded here and embedded verbatim under the artifact's "live" key. The go suite proves the same path against fixture harness directories with the same real binaries (internal/agent/skills/e2e_test.go); this file is the one run against the real ones.
recorded_by: the worker that ran the proof, transcribed from the run's captured stdout
commit_note: The tree that ran is committed as the implementation commit this evidence artifact accompanies; this SHA is the pre-commit HEAD anchor, not a checksum of the bytes that ran.

profile.name: daniel-skeleton
profile.note: The profile is vault-resident by design (<vault>/skills/homeplane.skills.toml). This run used the repository's reference copy via -profile because the task's boundaries make the real vault READ-ONLY for the implementer: the vault is a link SOURCE here and was never written. Daniel copies the reference file into the vault to make it resident.

harness_config_note: None. Both harnesses discover skills from a directory, so no config file is parsed or rewritten by this path and R5's merge machinery is not invoked.

assertions.claim: All three profile skills are linked into BOTH real harness skill directories.
Each harness entry is a symlink whose SKILL.md is the SAME FILE (inode) as the vault's; no independent editable copy exists.
assertions.evidence: every links[] entry has is_symlink=true, readlink into the vault, and same_file=true

assertions.claim: A fresh `claude 2.1.227` process enumerates all three skills in its system/init event.
A fresh `codex-cli 0.146.0` process enumerates all three skills, and reports the VAULT path as each one's locator.
Every pre-existing entry in both skill directories is byte-identical after the run; only the three new symlinks were added.

evidence.method: `ls -la` snapshot of both directories taken before the run and diffed after, excluding the three added entries

assertions.claim: A second `skills provision -verify` reports every skill unchanged, writes no link, and exits 0.

assertions.claim: Exactly the six created links are recorded in the 0600 ownership manifest, which is what makes `skills refresh` able to withdraw them and nothing else.
The skill the shipped profile marks unsupported (phone-home-coordinator) is absent from both real harness skill directories, and is refused even when a profile assigns it.

evidence.enforcement_test: internal/agent/skills/e2e_test.go TestRealVaultHarnessSpecificSkillsAreMarkedUnsupported provisions it deliberately against the real vault and asserts a profile-unsupported skip with no link created

caveats: The claude probe reads the system/init event and kills the process, so it makes NO model request. It is not otherwise side-effect-free: it starts the harness with the operator's real configuration, so Claude Code runs the operator's configured HOOKS (which is how the hook_started prelude ahead of the init event was found). The flags that suppress hooks (--bare, --safe-mode) also suppress the personal skills directory — verified — so a hook-free probe would enumerate nothing and prove nothing. The go suite avoids this by pointing the probe at a fixture configuration directory.

The `initiative-signal` classifier is conservative and over-marks: in this vault it holds back `ticktick`, whose matched line is the words "no cron". Every marking quotes its line, so a false positive is visible at a glance.

`phone-home-coordinator` trips NO mechanical rule — its text names no scheduler and no service manager. It is bound to the always-on server session, which is a judgement no classifier can make, so the shipped profile marks it `[unsupported]` with a reason and the provisioner ENFORCES that over any assignment (asserted against the real vault in TestRealVaultHarnessSpecificSkillsAreMarkedUnsupported). The exemplars that DO trip a rule are `hermes` (no SKILL.md), `restart` and `session-monitor`.
